$comment: U1.93's BTN1 via breached JLC's absolute minimum annular ring: 0.10 mm
against their published 0.15 mm floor (0.20 recommended). It came from U5,
which shrank the via to 0.5 mm to fit the 0.746 mm corridor between the
+3V3 and BTN2 pads -- solving a clearance problem by creating a ring problem.
The via cannot leave the pad: it is a 0.28 x 2.0 mm QFP pad on 0.5 mm pitch,
walled by a +3V3 diagonal 1.6 mm east and a GND trace 0.295 mm west, and the
0.22 mm gap between adjacent pads is below the 0.457 mm a track needs. Nor
can the via grow: the neighbouring pads cap it at 0.517 mm.
So shrink the DRILL instead. 0.5/0.2 gives exactly the 0.15 mm ring JLC
requires, and 0.2 mm is inside their 0.15-6.3 mm drill range -- though it is
below the 0.3 mm this project's rules file uses as its cost-neutral floor, so
expect it to be the one small-drill hit on the board.
RESIDUAL, recorded not fixed: it is still a via in an SMD pad. Tenting the
back stops solder dripping through but not wicking in. If the assembler
flags it, the remedy is JLCPCB's plugged/filled via option, or re-planning
the BTN1-4 and +3V3 escape fan in that corner.
